ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ \angle AOB : \angle BOC : \angle COD = 2 : 3 : 4$, the rays $OM$ and $ON$ bisect $ \angle AOB$ and $ \angle COD$ respectively. If $ \angle MON$ is a right angle, what is the measure of $ \angle COD$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle AOB=2x^\circ$, then $\angle BOC=3x^\circ$, $\angle COD=4x^\circ$,\\
since ray OM and ON bisect $\angle AOB$ and $\angle COD$ respectively,\\
therefore $\angle BOM= \frac{1}{2} \angle AOB=x^\circ$\\
$\angle CON= \frac{1}{2} \angle COD=2x^\circ$\\
since $\angle MON=90^\circ$\\
therefore $\angle CON+\angle BOC+\angle BOM=90^\circ$\\
therefore $2x+3x+x=90$\\
Solving for x, we get: $x=15$\\
therefore $\angle COD=4x =15^\circ \times 4=\boxed{60^\circ}$.

Since rays $OM$ and $ON$ bisect $\angle AOB$ and $\angle COD$ respectively, $\angle BOM=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOB=x^\circ$ and $\angle CON=\frac{1}{2}\angle COD=2x^\circ$. Since $\angle MON=90^\circ$, we have $\angle CON+\angle BOC+\angle BOM=90^\circ$, so $2x+3x+x=90$. Thus $x=15$, and $\angle COD=4x=60^\circ$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, all rays start from point O. Looking counterclockwise from the lower-right direction, they are in order OA, OM, OB, OC, ON, OD. The figure also marks ∠MON as a right angle, so ∠MON is composed of the three adjacent parts ∠MOB, ∠BOC, ∠CON.

Reasoning: It is known that ∠AOB : ∠BOC : ∠COD = 2 : 3 : 4. Let ∠AOB = 2x°, ∠BOC = 3x°, ∠COD = 4x°. Because OM bisects ∠AOB, ∠MOB = x°. Because ON bisects ∠COD, ∠CON = 2x°. From the adjacent relationship in the figure, ∠MON = ∠MOB + ∠BOC + ∠CON = x + 3x + 2x = 6x. Also because ∠MON is a right angle, 6x = 90, solving gives x = 15. Therefore ∠COD = 4x = 60°.
